title: Renewal & Expansion Check-in - Acme Payments
next_steps: Send updated pricing for 20% capacity increase and additional EU region
Share SOC 2 + ISO27001 pack and KMS architecture notes
Schedule 1-hour benchmark run with customer's PKB workloads (Liam) for week of 2026-06-22
Draft contract amendment for 12-month extension and reserved capacity terms
Follow up on PO timing and internal procurement approvals
action_items: Maya Chen — Send updated pricing and discount schedule — due 2026-06-18
Liam Patel — Prepare benchmark plan and test script — due 2026-06-19
Elena Morales — Share current throughput targets and peak RPS — due 2026-06-18
Carlos Reyes — Provide sample traffic profile and SSO metadata (SAML) — due 2026-06-18
summary: Renewal conversation focused on adding 20% dedicated capacity, enabling EU region, and drafting a 12-month contract amendment. Customer requested benchmarks against their peak card-clearing traffic and confirmation of SOC2/KMS controls before procurement sign-off.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We'll run 45 minutes. Quick intros?
[00:08] Rajiv Singh: Rajiv here, CFO, thanks.
[00:11] Elena Morales: Elena, CTO. Carlos on platform but he might speak more on infra.
[00:17] Carlos Reyes: Hey all, good to be here.
[00:20] Maya Chen: Great, Maya (Redwood) and Liam's on from SE. Quick agenda: renewal terms, capacity bump request, EU region add, and security follow-ups. Cool?
[00:30] Liam Patel: Yep, and we'll also talk benchmarks and runbook for the testing window.
[00:35] Rajiv Singh: We're trying to get visibility on cost if we move to more reserved capacity and what the commit gives us for discounts. Also timing — procurement wants an LOI by end of month.
[00:45] Maya Chen: Understood. So to summarize what we saw in usage — you spiked last month during the promo, average token throughput steady but peak RPS was about 2.6k, right Carlos?
[00:55] Carlos Reyes: Yeah roughly, with KV cache hits around 60%. The promo doubled our inference calls for about two hours. We want headroom so sub-second tails are consistent.
[01:05] Liam Patel: Good data point. For headroom we'd typically recommend a 15–25% reserved capacity bump depending on desired SLOs. You mentioned wanting 20%. With reserved capacity you get predictable throughput and a commit discount.
[01:20] Elena Morales: On the EU region — our data residency policy requires EU processing for EU-origin requests. Is that possible on Redwood Private or Hosted? What's the difference here for us?
[01:32] Maya Chen: Two paths. Hosted with EU region gives you processing in EU and we can enable tenancy isolation and bring-your-own-KMS for keys. Private (VPC) gives you more control — customer-managed networking, on-prem option. Most customers with strict residency pick Dedicated in EU or Private.
[01:46] Rajiv Singh: Pricing delta?
[01:48] Maya Chen: Slight premium for dedicated EU capacity vs hosted global routing — mostly driven by reserved GPU pool costs. We'll send a line-item in the updated quote.
[01:56] Carlos Reyes: For encryption — we need KMS integration details. We use CloudKeys/HSM and have policy that keys aren't exported.
[02:04] Liam Patel: We support external KMS via standard key-wrap and HSM integrations, and we can document the envelope encryption flow. I'll include the architecture diagram in the follow-up.
[02:13] Elena Morales: Also need SOC 2 and ISO packages for procurement.
[02:16] Maya Chen: Absolutely — we'll attach SOC 2 Type II and ISO docs; Liam will add the KMS notes and key rotation policy.
[02:23] Rajiv Singh: About the contract — we're looking at a 12-month extension with committed reserved capacity and a clause for burst credits. Can you do that?
[02:31] Maya Chen: Yes, we can draft an amendment — reserved capacity with burst allowances and automatic fallback to hosted models during outages if you opt-in. Pricing tiers will reflect the commitment.
[02:40] Liam Patel: Quick note on fallback — we can route to a cost-economy model variant in another region with preserved API semantics. It's not identical model but helps reliability.
[02:51] Carlos Reyes: Latency tradeoff? If we route out of EU during an outage, that's a problem for data residency compliance.
[02:57] Maya Chen: Right — that would be an opt-in behavior. For strict residency we'd recommend Dedicated in EU with cross-region failover only to EU-compatible fallback. We'll call out options in doc.
[03:10] Rajiv Singh: Procurement timeline — our legal wants to finish amendment review by 06/25. Can Redwood get pricing and docs by 06/18?
[03:18] Maya Chen: Yes, that's doable. We'll aim to send the revised quote and security pack by 06/18.
[03:23] Elena Morales: On benchmarks — we need a realistic test that mirrors our card-clearing pipeline. We want to run a 1-hour peak test. Liam, can you coordinate?
[03:32] Liam Patel: Absolutely. We'll need a sample traffic profile, peak QPS/RPS, input lengths, and KV hit rate. If Carlos can share anonymized logs or a trace, we can script the run.
[03:42] Carlos Reyes: I can export a 10-minute sample and a traffic histogram.
[03:46] Liam Patel: Perfect. We'll run it in your dedicated EU pool (or hosted EU if you prefer) and measure p95/p99 latencies and token cost.
[03:55] Rajiv Singh: One more ask — can committed capacity include a 10% overage credit bucket for sudden promos?
[04:02] Maya Chen: We can include a burst credit pool; exact size we'll propose in pricing. Typically customers pick a burst allowance equal to 10–25% of committed capacity.
[04:12] Elena Morales: Any differences between quantized model variants and full FP in terms of throughput? We may be sensitive to quality drop.
[04:20] Liam Patel: Yes, quantized variants can reduce GPU memory and increase throughput, but there is an accuracy delta. For production-critical scoring we typically recommend A/B tests; Redwood Optimize gives model/quant suggestions per workload.
[04:32] Carlos Reyes: Are there any outage SLAs tied to dedicated capacity? We need an SLA for 99.9% uptime and rollback plans for failed rollouts.
[04:40] Maya Chen: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and a rollback/automatic fallback policy. For rollouts we support canary deployments and automatic fallbacks to previous model or variant. We'll include the SLA language in the amendment.
[04:53] Rajiv Singh: Sounds good. Procurement will want line-item pricing per GPU equivalent or per-100k tokens.
[04:59] Maya Chen: We'll provide both views — reserved GPU equivalent + effective per-token cost at your average and peak usage.
[05:06] Elena Morales: On networking — do you support private peering to our VPCs?
[05:10] Liam Patel: Yes, for Private deployments and Dedicated we support VPC peering, private endpoints, and customer-managed subnets.
[05:16] Carlos Reyes: For SSO we need SAML metadata; also a single admin role for our security team.
[05:22] Maya Chen: We support SAML/SSO with SCIM provisioning and RBAC. We'll ask for the metadata in the follow-up.
[05:30] Rajiv Singh: OK, recap?
[05:33] Maya Chen: Recap: 1) Redwood sends updated pricing for +20% reserved capacity, EU region add, and burst credits by 06/18. 2) Liam schedules a 1-hour benchmark during week of 06/22 — need sample traffic by 06/18. 3) Security docs (SOC2/ISO/KMS) attached. 4) Redwood drafts contract amendment for 12 months. 5) Customer will aim to complete procurement review by 06/25.
[06:00] Elena Morales: That works, thanks.
[06:03] Carlos Reyes: I'll send the traffic sample and SAML metadata by EOD 06/18.
[06:07] Liam Patel: I'll draft the benchmark plan and share steps, test harness, and expected metrics.
[06:12] Maya Chen: Great, we'll follow up in email and log next steps in the CRM. Thanks everyone.
[06:17] Rajiv Singh: Thanks all.
[06:20] (call ends)

Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-transcriptions (e.g., "KV cache" sometimes transcribed as "K-V cash"), and speaker labels are accurate though informal. References: shared deck (link: https://redwood.example.com/decks/acme-renewal-0626), security pack (link: https://redwood.example.com/security/acme-pack), benchmark sheet (link: https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/acme-0626).
